a.label: Option A
a.notes: Narrative/product-first direction with broader positioning, editorial sections, and a more branded first impression.

b.label: Option B
b.notes: Workflow/operator-first direction with concrete steps, commands, proof points, and more task-oriented CTAs.

items.title: Developer CLI launch page
items.prompt: Create a landing page for ForgeCLI, a release cockpit for developer CLI projects. Compare a brand/product launch page against an install-first developer workflow page.

a.eyebrow: Command-line releases with a calmer rhythm
a.headline: Give every CLI release a launch surface.
a.summary: ForgeCLI turns binary publishing, changelog writing, and install docs into a single release moment.
a.proof: A product-first page for maintainers who want their tools to feel reliable before users run the first command.

b.headline: Build, sign, publish, and document a CLI release from one command.
b.summary: ForgeCLI gives maintainers a repeatable checklist for cross-platform binaries and GitHub releases.
b.proof: A developer-first page that shows the workflow before asking for trust.

items.title: Open source docs homepage
items.prompt: Create a landing page for DocsRail, an open source documentation homepage generator. Compare a documentation homepage against a contributor onboarding page.

a.headline: Turn a repo into a documentation homepage people can scan.
a.summary: DocsRail maps concepts, commands, examples, and release notes into a clear static docs entrypoint.
a.proof: Best when the main job is helping users understand what the project does and where to start.

b.headline: Give contributors the shortest path to a useful first PR.
b.summary: DocsRail can frame setup, architecture, starter issues, and review rules as one onboarding flow.
b.proof: Best when the docs need to activate contributors instead of only explaining the project.

items.title: AI notebook workspace
items.prompt: Create a landing page for LabSlate, an AI notebook workspace. Compare a visual research story against a practical experiment tracking workflow.

a.eyebrow: A visible trail for AI research
a.headline: Keep experiments, prompts, and decisions in one readable slate.
a.summary: LabSlate gives research work a visual memory so teams can revisit how conclusions emerged.
a.proof: A narrative page for researchers who want confidence that the workspace will preserve context.

b.headline: Compare prompts, runs, artifacts, and outcomes without rebuilding context.
b.summary: LabSlate organizes each experiment as a compact workflow: input, output, evidence, next action.
b.proof: A practical page for teams that need repeatable experiment review more than a research mood.

items.title: Plugin marketplace page
items.prompt: Create a landing page for PluginDock, a marketplace for runtime plugins. Compare discovery/browsing against trust-and-permissions-first install.

a.headline: Browse the plugins that make local agents more capable.
a.summary: PluginDock presents skills, MCP servers, and runtime commands as a searchable catalog.
a.proof: Best when the user needs breadth, categories, and fast discovery.

b.headline: See permissions, runtime access, and maintenance status before install.
b.summary: PluginDock makes each plugin explain what it can do, what it can touch, and how it updates.
b.proof: Best when trust, safety, and runtime compatibility matter more than browsing volume.

items.title: SaaS analytics product page
items.prompt: Create a landing page for Northstar Metrics. Compare an executive marketing page against an operator dashboard-oriented page.

a.headline: Know which product bets deserve the next sprint.
a.summary: Northstar Metrics turns user behavior into a calm story leaders can use for prioritization.
a.proof: A marketing-led page for buyers who need confidence, clarity, and a strategic promise.

b.headline: Scan goals, cohorts, and decisions in one operating view.
b.summary: Northstar Metrics reduces product analytics to the few numbers that change team action.
b.proof: An operator-led page for teams that need working surfaces, not another promise.

items.title: API observability launch page
items.prompt: Create a landing page for TraceHarbor. Compare a problem/incident story against a contract-debugging workflow page.

a.eyebrow: When APIs break, teams need a shared story
a.headline: Turn failing requests into incidents developers understand.
a.summary: TraceHarbor connects endpoint failures, customer impact, and deploy context into one narrative.
a.proof: Best when the page needs to communicate urgency and cross-team alignment.

b.eyebrow: Contract failures grouped by fix path
b.headline: Find the endpoint, schema, and deploy that caused the break.
b.summary: TraceHarbor gives API teams a debugging workflow organized around contract ownership.
b.proof: Best when the reviewer wants a concrete developer workflow and clear next actions.

items.title: Team knowledge base page
items.prompt: Create a landing page for FieldNotes. Compare a knowledge-memory story against a decision-record workflow.

a.headline: Keep the context behind work easy to find.
a.summary: FieldNotes gives teams a shared memory for projects, decisions, and source links.
a.proof: Best when the page needs to make knowledge feel durable and human.

b.eyebrow: Decision records with owners and expiry
b.headline: Write down what changed, who owns it, and when to revisit it.
b.summary: FieldNotes turns fuzzy team context into explicit decision records with accountable metadata.
b.proof: Best when the page should teach a repeatable team operating workflow.

items.title: Design review tool page
items.prompt: Create a landing page for FrameCheck. Compare a visual-quality brand page against a PR workflow tool page.

a.headline: Protect the interface your users actually see.
a.summary: FrameCheck turns responsive screenshots into a clear design review moment.
a.proof: Best when the page should feel visual, polished, and brand-led.

b.headline: Capture screenshots, compare breakpoints, and approve UI changes in PRs.
b.summary: FrameCheck makes visual regressions reviewable with concrete artifacts and comments.
b.proof: Best when the page needs to sell a workflow developers can add to CI.

items.title: Security changelog page
items.prompt: Create a landing page for PatchLedger. Compare a trust/compliance page against an advisory drafting workflow.

a.headline: Publish patch notes users can trust.
a.summary: PatchLedger helps teams communicate security changes with clarity and restraint.
a.proof: Best when the page should establish trust before describing the operational workflow.

b.headline: Explain affected versions, fixes, and user actions without leaking details.
b.summary: PatchLedger guides security teams through advisory drafts and release coordination.
b.proof: Best when the user needs a practical workflow for sensitive communication.

items.title: Customer onboarding page
items.prompt: Create a landing page for OnboardPath. Compare a customer-success promise page against a task-board implementation page.

a.headline: Make every onboarding feel guided from kickoff to launch.
a.summary: OnboardPath gives customer teams a calmer way to coordinate implementation work.
a.proof: Best when the page needs to reassure buyers and customer success leaders.

b.eyebrow: Implementation tasks with owners and blockers
b.headline: Track setup work, blockers, and launch readiness in one customer plan.
b.summary: OnboardPath turns onboarding into a visible task workflow for customers and internal teams.
b.proof: Best when the page should show exactly how a team operates the product.

items.title: Local automation tool page
items.prompt: Create a landing page for DeskPilot. Compare a local-first privacy page against a recipe-driven automation page.

a.eyebrow: Automation that stays on your machine
a.headline: Run desktop routines without handing work to the cloud.
a.summary: DeskPilot keeps file, form, and export automations local and inspectable.
a.proof: Best when trust, privacy, and control are the primary concern.

b.headline: Turn weekly exports, forms, and file cleanup into one-click routines.
b.summary: DeskPilot gives operators recipe templates they can adapt without writing scripts.
b.proof: Best when the page should make the product feel immediately useful to non-developers.

items.title: Developer onboarding docs page
items.prompt: Create a landing page for StartHere. Compare a welcoming onboarding page against a first-PR execution page.

a.eyebrow: A better first day in the repo
a.headline: Help new engineers understand where they are.
a.summary: StartHere creates a welcoming map of setup, architecture, and team conventions.
a.proof: Best when the page should reduce anxiety and orient new contributors.

b.eyebrow: From clone to first merged PR
b.headline: Give every new engineer a verified path to contribution.
b.summary: StartHere turns setup checks, code map, and starter issues into a first-PR workflow.
b.proof: Best when onboarding success means shipping a safe first change.
